newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore cuts 1996 tourism growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: Singapore cuts 1996 tourism growth forecast.

text.p: Singapore has revised its 1996 visitor arrival growth forecast to two percent, down from an earlier 3-5 percent estimate, a Singapore Tourist Promotion Board (STPB) spokeswoman said on Thursday.

The forecast was based on visitor arrivals over the first 10 months of this year after July, August and September registered declines of 3.7 percent, 4.8 percent, and 5.9 percent, respectively, over the same months in 1995.
However "the underlying trends in visitor traffic to Singapore remain positive," the spokeswoman said.
"One of the immediate tactical measures to address the slowdown is to fine-tune and intensify our marketing efforts," she said.

Singapore's Straits Times newspaper quoted travel agents earlier this month as saying some tourists were opting to go to Hong Kong over Singapore, attracted by advertisements and press reports and by the approach of the 1997 handover of the British colony to China.
